London, 16<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**General Motors** has told U.S. dealers it is accelerating its timetable for closing about 1,700 dealerships as it rushes to meet a June 1 deadline to restructure under U.S. government oversight, people with knowledge of the discussions said.   GM executives also said about 200 dealerships had closed in the first quarter.  The issue of how many U.S. dealerships GM can support has been one of the hot-button issues for U.S. officials as they drive GM toward a stepped-up restructuring that many observers have now concluded will include a bankruptcy filing.  As a result, GM officials have told dealers that they would identify underperforming locations and could move to terminate franchise agreements by June 1, a dealer who had received such a notice said on Wednesday. 

GM is counting on the spin-off or closure of its Saturn and Hummer brands -- combined with dealership closures because of declining business conditions and tight credit -- to deliver about half of its targeted cuts, according to the dealer.  For the remainder, GM is preparing to terminate franchise agreements without the kind of payouts that it made when it shut down its Oldsmobile division and closed some 2,800 dealerships. That process cost GM more than $1 billion. 

## _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**General Motors** , facing a June 1 U.S.-backed bankruptcy, may drop its Pontiac and GMC brands as part of broader cost-cutting moves, people familiar with the discussions said. GM’s Chevrolet, Cadillac and Buick brands are likely safe, said the people.   Shedding Pontiac or GMC would mean a deeper bite into GM’s portfolio of eight U.S. brands than in its Feb. 17 blueprint for keeping $13.4 billion in federal loans. GM said then it would keep Chevrolet, Cadillac, Buick and GMC and retain Pontiac as a niche line while selling or closing Hummer, Saab and Saturn. 

## _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**In the UK** , consumers are to be offered incentives of up to £5,000 to purchase an electric car under government plans to be unveiled today that will also see the creation of electric car cities across the country and the launch of large-scale experiments with ultra-green vehicles. The proposals are part of a £250m strategy spelling out a revolution in Britain’s road transport network based on ultra-low carbon vehicles.  The cash incentive for consumers would be available to offset the higher upfront costs of electric cars, in particular the price of the batteries in modern vehicles. How the money would be distributed is yet to be decided but Geoff Hoon, Transport Secretary, said it would be available only to people buying cars that ran entirely, or for the vast majority of their time, on electricity. The scheme, which would be enforced by setting a ceiling for the amount of CO2 a car emits, will become operational in 2011.  Car manufacturers are a key part of the strategy: £100m will be available for research to car makers.

“What we want to see is the UK firmly in the lead in the manufacturing sense because we want to ensure the incentives ... benefit, broadly, manufacturing in the UK,” said Hoon. 

## _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Japan’s Takashimaya** department store has  a 10 million yen (100,000 USD) CD on sale called “Woman, Sweet 10 Diamonds”, made with a platinum case and studded with a total of 10 2-carat diamonds, produced by Universal Music and Japanese jeweller Nagahori in Tokyo. Universal Music unveiled the “world’s most expensive CD” for its 10th commemorate album showcasing 18 songs by female vocalists.
